title: The Akal Takht rebuilt
hookLine: Sikhs pulled down the government-repaired Akal Takht and rebuilt it by volunteer labor

cards: A new building stands where a broken one stood. The walls are straight, the paint is fresh, the dome is whole. And the people it was built for won't accept it.
They gather with hammers and baskets and take it apart, brick by brick, by hand. Then they start again, from the ground, carrying the new bricks themselves. It sounds like waste.
To the Sikhs who did it at the Akal Takht, after June, it was the only way the building could be theirs again. The way they did it is today's word: kar seva.

teach.h: THE THRONE OF THE TIMELESS ONE.
teach.b: First, the throne. The Akal Takht, the throne of the Timeless One, stands facing the Darbar Sahib in Amritsar, the seat from which Sikh decisions and edicts go out. This path has met it before.
In June it was badly damaged in the fighting. Second, the repair.
The government had it repaired quickly, with a Nihang leader, Baba Santa Singh, at the head of the work.
But to the Sikh bodies that speak for the panth, a throne repaired by the government that had broken it was not a throne.
They called it the government's building, and the Akal Takht later censured Santa Singh for his part in it. Third, the rebuilding.
Kar seva volunteers pulled the repaired building down and rebuilt the Akal Takht. Kar means work; seva means selfless service.
Led by kar seva teams, volunteers carried earth, bricks and mortar on their heads, the way kar seva is done. No wage. No contract.
At Ang 286 of the Guru Granth Sahib, in the Sukhmani, Guru Arjan says that the one who serves without wanting anything in return reaches the Lord.
In Sikh teaching, seva is not a side activity. It is a way the hands pray. And for a throne that stands for the panth's own voice, only the panth's own hands would do.

how: Sikhs remember the rebuilding of the Akal Takht by kar seva as a statement that the panth's throne must be built by the panth itself; kar seva volunteers still build and clean gurdwaras by hand.

volunteer work that builds and cleans the Gurus' places

games.q: the government has repaired the broken Akal Takht. it looks whole. what do the Sikhs do?
o: pull it down and rebuild it with their own hands.
games.why: they pulled the repaired building down and rebuilt it by kar seva, volunteers carrying the bricks themselves.

practice: Picture where an hour of your hands could help: a food bank, a cleanup, a gurdwara kitchen, a neighbor's garden, a shelter.

Breathe in and see yourself arriving; breathe out and see the work, carrying, washing, sweeping, stirring, with no one paying you and no one thanking you. If you pray, let Waheguru go with the picture.

wordCard.voice: Kar seva. Kar is work, seva is selfless service: volunteer labor that builds and cleans the Gurus' places, and that rebuilt the Akal Takht. Today's word.

orig.note: kar is work; seva is selfless service. volunteer labor for the Guru's house.

carryVoice: Your line: built by volunteers. Just hands, the panth's own, carrying the bricks. A new week begins.
